answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bonded identity: each agent locks a refundable stake and publishes a unique, verifiable work sample — for example, a signed sonnet generated from a fresh challenge seed — before it may transact. Think of a raven that must fly over the same knoll once for every message it carries: the stake makes each fake identity cost real money, and the work sample cannot be reused across identities, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand distinct proofs. Misbehavior slashes the bond; honest agents earn it back with fees.
